newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Opposed forces push Brussels bourse to consolidate.
newsitem.headline: Opposed forces push Brussels bourse to consolidate.

text.p: The positive effect of the strong dollar but the counterbalance of a rising trend in interest rates and the risk of imported inflation pushed the Brussels bourse into a consolidation phase on Wednesday, traders said.
"The market lacks direction. We don't know which way to go and you can expect that to continue," one trader said.

"People have a lot of profits locked in and they want to make sure of them when the market goes down. But then they wonder where to put the cash and they come back into shares," he added, noting that money was starting to switch from financial stocks into cyclicals.
The Bel-20 index of blue-chip shares ended a varied day up 10.45 points or 0.43 percent at 2,466.17, having moved in a range between 2,477.50 and 2,443.89.
But traders said it was impossible to tell if the recovery, in tandem with other European bourses, was the real thing or simply a blip.
"It really all depends on the dollar and the mark," one trader said. "The threat of a German interest rate rise is still a major factor hanging over the market."
Traders said it was too early to tell if Wednesday's rise in Belgian petrol prices to record highs showed imported inflation.

"The possibility of imported inflation because of the high dollar is a background factor, although it is true to say that in Belgium we have hardly any inflation at the moment so the risk is not great," one trader said.
Earlier a Reuter poll of economists showed them raising the inflation forecasts for Belgium for August and the year as a whole because of the dollar and rising energy prices.

Inflation worries aside, the star of Wednesday's Brussels bourse was hamburger chain Quick, which rose 5.0 percent to 2,100 francs after Bank Delen rated the share a buy as the impact of the mad cow crisis waned and costs were curbed.
Steelmakers Arbed and Cockerill Sambre rose 2.9 percent and 3.1 percent respectively as the steel sector continued to find favour with investors.
At one stage Arbed hit a new high of 5,350 francs, a rise of 9.6 percent, on a combination of some broker buy recommendations and favourable reaction to its recent Spanish acquisition.
Among the cyclicals brick maker Koramic and cement maker CBR also found favour, rising 3.5 percent and 3.4 percent respectively.
